elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Subparagraph 18.8: "Teleglobe USA Inc. (the 'Customer') may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time, whether during or after the Initial Period". In this multi-party consortium instrument the operative exit unit is a Party's "participation", so termination of participation is the functional equivalent of terminating the Agreement as to Customer; the right is unconditional ("for convenience at any time") and runs to Customer alone. There are no Order Forms in this structure, so that limb is inapplicable.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 18.8: "by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties" — exactly 30 days, in writing, no additional consent, Management Committee approval or unanimity condition attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.8: "the other Parties shall refund to the Customer, pro rata, any charges prepaid by the Customer in respect of the period after the effective date of such termination." The word "pro rata" is express (not inferred from the post-termination period alone) and the payer obligation is placed on the counterparty side.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained 18.1: "any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice" — the effective date is expressly tied to the end of/after the 25-year Initial Period, so no counterparty convenience exit exists mid-term; 18.2 requires unanimous written agreement of all Parties for any termination during the Initial Period. 18.8 is drafted as additive ("In addition to Subparagraph 18.1") and grants the new right only to Customer, so it does not create a counterparty exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 18.8 sets 30 days, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (and is the better preferred-level outcome). Fallback is therefore incomplete, but the preferred level is complete, so this does not defeat position-completeness.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: 18.8 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment on Customer. 18.4's "No credit for capital costs" rule is expressly keyed to terminations "in accordance with Subparagraph 18.1", not to 18.8, and is a denial of credit rather than an exit fee.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Retained 18.1 confines any Party's unilateral exit to "the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; the termination effective date is expressly anchored to the end of the committed term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice", which exceeds 90 days.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the inserted 18.8 supplies the Customer-only convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and the express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period, while retained 18.1/18.2 already deny the counterparties any mid-term convenience exit.

Minimality holds: the redline is a single concise insertion (18.8) for a right that was wholly missing; nothing favourable is deleted or paraphrased, 18.1, 18.2, 18.4 and 18.7 are left intact, and the insertion adds no extras (no survival tail, no expense or damages language, no procedure) beyond the four checklist elements. The phrase "whether during or after the Initial Period" is necessary scope, not an extra.

Intent preserved: the clause is expressly additive to 18.1, leaves the other Parties' exit mechanics, the Management Committee route in 18.2 and the Schedule B apportionment references untouched, and creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference. Drafting note only (not a defect requiring repair): 18.4 (no capital-cost credit) and 18.7 (continuing liabilities) are keyed to terminations "pursuant to Subparagraph 18.1", so a 18.8 exit falls outside both; if the counterparty raises this, expect a request to extend those cross-references, which would be neutral-to-adverse for us.

Deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" appears to be a wording-pattern artefact (the regex likely looks for "terminate this Agreement" whereas 18.8 says "terminate its participation in this Agreement"); in substance the Customer convenience right is present and unconditional in the rendered operative text, and the coverage and minimality gates both pass.

Fallback level is incomplete solely because the 30-day notice is shorter than the 60–90 day band; since that is more favourable to us and the preferred level is fully met, no repair is needed. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation, because the unredlined Paragraph 18 gave us no convenience exit in a 25-year term (walk-away territory) and no capped early-termination fee.
